newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian stocks steady in thin volume.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian stocks steady in thin volume.

text.p: Shares on Jordan's stock exchange rose a slight 0.14 percent at the start of weekly trade on Saturday with minimal buying activity in a liquidity squeezed market, dealers said.
The official Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose 0.21 points to 153.60 points.
Low turnover of 323,980 dinars ($457,598) was dominated again by investor demand on a handful of stock expected to post healthy 1996 earnings.

"Buying was limited to a number of stock, with cash short investors looking for firms that are going to distribute dividends on 1996 results," said Ibrahim Odeh of Wataniyah Financial Services brokerage firm.

Odeh said lack of liquidity appeared to be the main reason why trading has plummeted over the last few weeks. Few small investors are being encouraged to enter in the absence of institutional and foreign buyers to buttress volume, he added.
A few banks, Bank of Jordan, Jordan National Bank and Housing Bank, were the focus of some attention in otherwise thin across-the-board trade.

The bourse has also not been helped by many investors in a wait-and-see mood over the fate of Arab-Israeli peace making. A barometer of sentiment in the Middle East peace process, the market is highly sensitive to regional tension, brokers said.
Jordan Industrial Resources, which was the busiest stock on healthy 1996 results, rose 0.04 percent to 1.39 dinars in trade worth 61,097 dinars.
The second busiest, Jordan Cement Factories, rose 0.02 dinars to 3.63 dinars in trade worth 48,590 dinars as the stock continued to attract some institutional buying.
Overall falling shares outnumbered gainers by 12 to 13. Another five shares traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 most-traded shares on the exchange rose 0.13 percent to 80.53 points, 3.43 percent down from the start of the year.
